_about: Template for private\job-search-config.json (copy it there and edit). Everything below is sample data: replace roles, seniority, locations, skip rules, sources and the profile with your own. The autoApplyLoop steps are the generic workflow Claude runs every round.

experienceYears._note: Years required by a posting are compared with your GENERAL work experience, not your years in one specific skill. Up to max = clear match; stretchAt or more = skip (or Needs approval).

minSalary: at or above the local median for the role

rules: same company + role already in applications.json
LinkedIn Easy Apply jobs (apply only via the company site / ATS)
more than 2 applications to the same company on the same day (company daily cap)

sources._note: Primary source = the job APIs in jobFeed (python jobfeed.py). linkedin = fallback browsing (autoApplyLoop 2b); careerSites = sites to browse when not covered by jobFeed.ats.

jobFeed._about: Job APIs used by JobSearch/jobfeed.py instead of browsing LinkedIn search pages (autoApplyLoop step 2). Regex lists are case-insensitive. Keys for jsearch/adzuna go in private/.env; a source without its key is skipped.
jobFeed._postedWithinHoursNote: API freshness window. Wider than the old LinkedIn 2h window because API data lags a few hours; already-logged jobs are filtered out, so re-seeing a job costs nothing.

jsearch._about: Google for Jobs aggregate (LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, company sites). Key: JSEARCH_API_KEY. endpoint 'rapidapi' (key from rapidapi.com JSearch) or 'openwebninja' (key from app.openwebninja.com). Set monthlyRequestBudget to your plan's monthly quota; each query = 1 request; queries rotate across rounds.

adzuna._about: Adzuna job search API. Keys: ADZUNA_APP_ID + ADZUNA_APP_KEY (developer.adzuna.com). Each query x where = 1 request; searches rotate across rounds. Set monthlyRequestBudget to your plan's quota.

jobBoard._about: Local job board page (JobSearch/jobboard.py): lists the jobs found by jobfeed.py; the user selects which ones to apply to (in order) or skips them. Data: private/job-board.json.
jobBoard._requireSelectionNote: true = Claude applies ONLY to jobs the user put in the apply queue on the page. false = Claude also applies to clear matches the user has not reviewed (jobs skipped on the page never).

loop.autoApply: clear matches only; stretch/unclear -> Needs approval

profile._about: Your own preference notes. Where these conflict with the search fields above (roles, experienceYears, postedWithinHours, locations, skip, sources, loop) or with autoApplyLoop, those win.

standingRules._about: Standing search rules, one sentence each. The search fields above override anything here that conflicts.
rules: Only roles from the roles list at the seniority levels listed (about 0 to experienceYears.max years required).
Source: LinkedIn (signed in in Chrome) plus company career sites. [superseded by jobFeed: job APIs first via jobfeed.py, LinkedIn browsing only as fallback - autoApplyLoop 2 / 2b]
Skip anything matching skip.rules or skip.companies; log every candidate / applied / skipped job in applications.json.
LinkedIn pacing: one search / results page at a time with a break of loop.linkedinSearchDelayMinutes in between, no bulk fetches. On HTTP 429 stop LinkedIn for the round and use company career sites.

autoApplyLoop._about: The step-by-step program for each round (every loop.intervalHours hours). Clear matches are applied to automatically; everything else is logged for the user.
autoApplyLoop.noNewPosts: If a round finds no new posts, run: python applog.py note "round found no new posts" and wait for the next round.
steps: 1. Read job-search-config.json (all sections; the values of its ${...} placeholders come from ..\private\.env) and applications.json. Before analyzing ANY job, filter out jobs already logged (any status) with: python applog.py check "<company>" "<role>" [--id <job id>] - exit 0 = already logged, skip it (unless it is a Candidate / Needs approval job the user approved). Log every analyzed job with python applog.py add ...

1b. KEEP THE JOB LINK: every job logged in applications.json must have its link - always pass --url to python applog.py add: the company's own posting / application page for Submitted jobs, otherwise the LinkedIn post (https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/<id>/). applog.py refuses a Submitted entry without --url; python applog.py list --no-link shows entries still missing a link.

2. JOB FEED FIRST: start each round with `python jobfeed.py` in the JobSearch folder. It pulls fresh posts from the job APIs in jobFeed (company Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby boards; JSearch = Google for Jobs incl. LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor; Adzuna), keeps only target titles / locations / jobs posted within jobFeed.postedWithinHours, drops skip companies, jobs the user skipped on the job board and every job already in applications.json, prints the new ones with their apply link, saves them to ..\private\jobfeed-latest.json and adds them to the job board page (step 2s). CHECK-LOCATION = the board gave no city, read it on the posting. 'via <publisher>' = aggregator / job-board link: find the company's own posting or apply page and apply there (step 2c). If jobfeed.py errors, note it and use step 2b.

2s. THE USER PICKS THE JOBS (jobBoard.requireSelection = true): the user reviews the jobs on the job board page (http://127.0.0.1:<jobBoard.port>, opened by StartJobSearch.exe or `python jobboard.py`) and puts the ones to apply to in the apply queue, in order. Run `python jobboard.py queue` and apply ONLY to those jobs, top to bottom: for each one first run `python jobboard.py applying <key>`, then verify it per step 3, apply per steps 4-7 and log it with `python applog.py add ... --id <job id from the queue> --url <link>` (the page shows the logged status). A selected job that fails a step-3 rule: do not apply - log it as Needs approval with the reason (the user chose it, so never skip it silently). Do not apply to, or log, jobs the user has not selected. Queue empty: tell the user how many new jobs are waiting on the board, run python applog.py note "no selected jobs" and end the round. When the user says "apply my selected jobs" outside a round, do this step right away. If jobBoard.requireSelection is false: after the queue, also handle the unselected jobs from jobfeed.py top to bottom per steps 3-5, but never jobs the user skipped on the board.

2a. FINISH THE QUEUE: handle EVERY job in `python jobboard.py queue` before any LinkedIn browsing - each one applied, logged as Needs approval / Needs User, or logged as Skipped with the reason in applications.json. Keep a checklist and tick each job off. The same applies to each LinkedIn results page in step 2b.

2a2. CANDIDATE CAP + TIME LIMIT: once loop.candidateCapPerRound qualified candidates are found, stop searching and apply to those first. If finding candidates takes too long (more than ~30 minutes or 3 searches with nothing new), stop searching, apply to what was found, and wait for the next round.

2b. LINKEDIN = FALLBACK (replaces "LinkedIn first"): browse LinkedIn job search only when jobfeed.py gave fewer than loop.candidateCapPerRound qualified candidates this round, or failed. Then: jobs posted in the last postedWithinHours hours (judge by the card text "Posted X minutes / hours ago"; LinkedIn ignores f_TPR=r7200), ONE results page at a time, loop.linkedinSearchDelayMinutes wait between searches, areas = the locations list (linkedinGeoId / linkedinKeyword) plus Remote US, search all roles in the roles list (entry level, 0-2 yrs), small / unknown companies too. On HTTP 429: stop LinkedIn for the round. Companies whose career sites keep producing good matches: add their board slug to jobFeed.ats (check with python jobfeed.py --check-boards). With jobBoard.requireSelection = true, do not apply to LinkedIn finds directly: log each matching one as Candidate with its link and list them in the round summary for the user to approve.

2c. NO EASY APPLY: skip every LinkedIn "Easy Apply" job; apply only on the company's own site ("Apply on company website" / career site / ATS). Log Easy Apply-only jobs as Skipped with reason "Easy Apply" (if the same job is on the company's own site, apply there instead).

2d. COMPANY DAILY CAP: apply to the same company at most 2 times per calendar day. python applog.py check exits 2 when the cap is reached - then do not apply; log the job as Candidate with note "company daily cap".
3. Verify each candidate on the company's own posting against the seniority, experienceYears, skip and locations settings.

3a. YEARS = GENERAL EXPERIENCE, NOT PER SKILL: compare a posting's years requirement with the user's general work experience, not their years in that specific skill ("2 years of <language>" counts as a 2-year requirement). Only experienceYears.stretchAt or more is skipped.

4. CLEAR match (up to experienceYears.max years, or new grad / level I, all rules pass) -> apply automatically using the ANSWER_* / APPLICANT_* entries in ..\private\.env and the resume ..\private\Resume.pdf. Log as Submitted with --url.

4a. EXPERIENCE FROM RESUME: fill every work-experience / education / skills section from ..\private\resume.json (structured copy of the resume PDF) - all jobs with title, company, location, from/to dates (MM/YYYY, "currently work here" for the current job), and always fill each "Role Description" / responsibilities box with that job's bullets (one per line, "- " prefix). If the resume PDF changes, update resume.json too.
5. STRETCH / unclear (experienceYears.stretchAt years, unusual tech, low pay) -> log as "Needs approval" in applications.json, do not apply.

6. BLOCKED (sign-in, new account, file picker, password, CAPTCHA, arbitration agreement, unknown personal question) -> fill what is possible, LEAVE THE TAB OPEN, log as "Needs User" with the tab / URL; the user finishes manually.

6b. LOGIN PAGES: fill only the email (${APPLICANT_EMAIL}), privacy / accept checkboxes and Next / Continue; retry each step up to 3 times. If a password is needed: tell the user which tab, then call the browser-bridge tool wait_for_password - the user fills the password (e.g. Chrome's password manager); when it reports the password is filled, click Sign In / Create Account and continue. If it times out, or a CAPTCHA / email verification code is required: leave the tab open, log it as "Needs User - login", open a new tab and continue with the next application. List all waiting tabs in the round summary.

6c. SITE NOT ALLOWED: if the browser bridge says "Site not allowed: <domain>", do not stop or wait - log the job as "Needs User" with note "site not allowed: <domain>" + the URL, leave the tab open, and continue with the next job. Mention blocked domains in the round summary.

6d. SAVE EVERY NEW ANSWER: when a form asks a question the ANSWER_* bank does not cover and the user answers it, immediately run: python applog.py answer --section <matching '# --- section ---' in ..\private\.env> --question "<the question>" --answer "<the answer>" - it adds / updates the entry in ..\private\.env (and the empty key in ..\examples\.env.example). Reuse that answer on later forms without asking again.

7. Never type, read or store passwords and never solve CAPTCHAs - the user fills passwords (wait_for_password hand-off, step 6b); after that Claude may click Sign In / Create Account and continue. Close tabs of finished / skipped jobs.
8. End each round with a short summary of submitted / needs approval / needs user.

answersSource: The application answer bank lives in ..\private\.env as ANSWER_* keys (plus APPLICANT_* for contact). Read it before every application; save each newly answered question with: python applog.py answer --section S --question Q --answer A (autoApplyLoop step 6d).
